summary: The note describes how the Arabian Peninsula was divided into four distinct regions before the modern era: Hejaz (Tihamah), Najd (Al-Yamama), Southern Arabia (Hadhramaut), and Eastern Arabia. It explains which modern countries and areas make up each region, noting that Hejaz and Najd form most of Saudi Arabia. It is a short overview of the peninsula's historical regional divisions.
one_line: Overview of the four pre-modern regions of the Arabian Peninsula and the modern countries and areas they cover.
key_facts: Before the modern era, the Arabian Peninsula was divided into four distinct regions.
The four pre-modern regions were Hejaz (Tihamah), Najd (Al-Yamama), Southern Arabia (Hadhramaut), and Eastern Arabia.
Hejaz and Najd make up most of Saudi Arabia.
Southern Arabia consists of Yemen and some parts of Saudi Arabia, namely Najran, Jizan, and Asir.
Southern Arabia also includes Oman's Dhofar region.
Eastern Arabia consists of the entire coastal strip of the Persian Gulf.
